newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end at day's highs, boosted by Btps.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end at day's highs, boosted by Btps.

text.p: Italian stocks ended at the day's highs with gains of around three percent on Tuesday, boosted by soaring Italian bond futures with the December Liffe Btp contract hitting a new historic high.

Dealers said traded volumes were not enormous but interest had returned to several blue chip stocks which had been neglected in the recent rush to buy shares in energy giant ENI after the Italian Treasury sold a second tranche.
The all-share Mibtel index closed 2.72 percent higher at 9,895 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended 3.11 percent up at 14,897.
Fiat SpA shares firmed strongly in late trade after recent session losses, closing 5.54 percent up at 4,193 lire, just off its day's high of 4,200 lire, in fair volume of 6.8 million shares.
Traders said Fiat and other blue chip stocks were beginning "to breathe again" after the heavy buying of ENI.
Also helping was the recent billion dollar market debut of Fiat's New Holland NV and market talk of restructuring in Fiat's chemical sector.
ENI ended 2.27 percent higher at 7,390 lire, the most heavily traded stock with over 22 million shares changing hands.

Fiat group units Snia Bpd and Sorin Biomedica were in the spotlight for the second day with some analysts seeing a revival of talk Fiat might be wanting to restructure its chemical division. Sorin heads up the bio-engineering activities of chemical holding Snia Bpd. There was no comment from Fiat.
Snia ended 8.11 pct up at 1,319 and Sorin 1.59 up at 5,236.

Shares in Carlo De Benedetti's holding Compagnie Industriali Riunite SPA (CIR), which holds 14 percent of the troubled Olivetti group, spiked up nine percent in Milan on early news it was selling its stake in French unit Valeo.
CIR pared gains to close 2.66 percent up at 742 lire.
